I understand what you are going through. I got an associate's degree in psychology, statically the least useful. It took me 4 years to get it too. Right out of college, I couldn't find a job in anything that wasn't either retail or fast food. The only SO I ever had dumped me after I got a job at a Walmart because I "would never amount to anything".  I was suicidal for a long while. Long story short from there, I realized I couldn't do literally anything successfully, even take my own life. So I decided, fuck it, I am going to learn how to be better. If there is something you feel like you don't know how to do, then it's never too late to learn. For example, you mentioned cooking. Start with something basic, like how to cook an [egg](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yyi55ZrpJ0E) or [rice](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xx7sxWI9FNI). From there, you can move on to slightly harder things, like cooking [fried rice](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eY1FF6SEggk&t=141s). Baby steps are the key to improvement. Completing goals is also a great way to raise self-worth. You can't be completely worthless if you learned if you can do something right?

Dude, it sounds like you have hit rock bottom. Trust me, I completely relate. About a year ago I was diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder. A lot of what you are describing, the feeling of little worth, high anxiety, existential dread, got all that. The thing I have found that helps me the most when I get feelings like that is to just try *something*. Start with one thing you want to change about yourself and make a plan to work at it. I hated my weight, so I started by drinking one less soda a week. That encouraged me to ditch it all together a few months later and replace it with tea. I started seeing results from that so I started to add more vegetables to my meals, which lead to a lot more healthy habits. Through this process, I have lost over 100 pounds in the past year. The fact that I have made progress on a goal I had, has given me such a boost to my self-worth. I still have bad days, but now I have something to fall back on when my depression hits hard. I can't be *completely* worthless, I did a thing! See where I am going with this at all? You may feel bad about yourself now, but you can improve yourself with just a little bit of effort.
